summary: Miles is tiny, bony, moves with difficulty, and does not feel pain. He is also the funniest, most devious kid in the dorm and he knows exactly how he looks to strangers. When he senses someone is uncomfortable with him he dials every eccentricity up to eleven and watches them run. A lot of what Miles does is on purpose. Treating it all as distress or disability misses him completely — and teaches him that the performance works. Treat it as humor when it's humor, as a safety problem when it's a safety problem, and keep a straight face.
strengths: deeply attached to his one-to-one and she to him
wants to learn physical things (skateboarding) despite his body
interests: skateboarding — being held and run along on the board

expressive.voiceStyle: quiet, sing-song, deadpan. 'Nice soft hair… nice soft hair.' He knows it's funny.

registers.name: the creep-out act (leg-hair rubbing, exaggerated stares, sudden appearances)
registers.ifUnauthorized: Anyone can be a target. The right response is flat and friendly; the wrong response is flinching, which is the payoff.

bestWith: talking to him like the sharp 13-year-old he is
plain safety rules stated once, as facts
avoid: pretending you didn't notice a stunt

lexicon.form: sneaks up at bunk check and strokes your leg hair saying 'nice soft hair… nice soft hair'

meanings.gloss: Testing you / making you jump because it's funny

lexicon.notes: He does it to people who will flinch. Don't flinch. 'Hi Miles. Bed.' ends it; a shriek guarantees a repeat.

lexicon.form: exaggerates his gait, stare, and mannerisms when a stranger looks uncomfortable

meanings.gloss: You're scared of me, so I'll give you something to be scared of — and I'm in charge of that, not you
Hurt by how people look at him (underneath the joke)

lexicon.form: bites someone — hard, fast, from close range, often while they're resting

meanings.gloss: A stunt that crossed the line; he is testing what happens

lexicon.notes: Hard no, stated once, flat. Then move on. The reaction is the reward; the boundary is the message.

lexicon.form: drags the skateboard to you and stands on it, holding his arms out

meanings.gloss: Hold me and run me around on the board

lexicon.notes: This is the real Miles. He never falls when held. Say yes often.

lexicon.form: announces 'I got hurt' or shows an injury, calm, watching your face

meanings.gloss: Someone will get in trouble now — and I know it
Genuine injury he can't feel and wants checked

lexicon.notes: Both can be true at once. ALWAYS check the injury — he cannot feel it, so it may be worse than it looks. Keep your face boring while you do.

triggers.trigger: unsupervised access to outlets, forks, heights, anything that would hurt a kid who could feel it
earlySigns: slides out of sight (under the table)
triggers.escalation: fork in the outlet; smashing himself into things; crawls somewhere he can't get out of
whatHelps: eyes on him always; if you can't see him, find him
outlet covers in every room he uses
give him a real, slightly dangerous-feeling job (pushing the cart fast) so he doesn't invent one
whatMakesItWorse: a big reaction when he's caught

motifs.meaning: I see you / the stunt is noted

motifs.cue: 'No.' once, then move on, no discussion

people.name: Lena
people.notes: loves him; the person he performs least for

people.name: Casey
people.notes: skateboard runner; got bitten once, unimpressed, still friends

goals.text: Miles will get a laugh from staff with a joke that isn't a stunt, daily.
goals.measure: staff log: verbal jokes vs. physical stunts

goals.text: Daily full skin check by nurse; every 'I got hurt' gets examined, calmly, every time.

safetyAlerts: Congenital insensitivity to pain: he cannot feel injury. Check every bump; a daily skin check is medical, not optional.
Will deliberately hurt himself to provoke a reaction (fork in outlet). Outlet covers, eyes on him, boring face.

fit.note: Communication is not Miles's deficit. The tool here is for the partner: telling performance from need, and keeping him safe without rewarding the stunt.
